comment: The counterfactual of wages-and-married-child-refund-only-single, one answer apart: the dependent and their spouse ARE required to file the joint return, so the joint-return test FAILS and the person is not claimed. Blessed from the pinned engine, hand-checked to the dollar against a measured table: line 16 does not move (3,665 — the tax before credits is the same return), line 24 rises the whole 2,200 child tax credit to 3,665, and line 33 loses the 345 earned income credit (6,345 -> 6,000), leaving overpaid 2,335. A failed joint-return test is a COMPUTED outcome, not a refusal and not a knockout — the engine models it, and the refund-only answer is not asked because the chain does not reach it.
